title: Decentralized Peer-to-Peer File Distribution Engine in Go with Kademlia DHT & Rarest-First Swarm Scheduling
problem: Centralized file distribution architectures suffer from bandwidth exhaustion, single-point-of-failure bottlenecks, and exponential egress bandwidth costs when distributing large software packages to thousands of clients. Naive peer-to-peer implementations experience severe swarm churn when peers disconnect mid-download, choke on corrupted binary blocks due to lack of cryptographic verification, and fail to discover peers when central tracker servers are unreachable. This project builds a decentralized peer-to-peer (P2P) file distribution engine in Go inspired by the BitTorrent protocol. The engine splits files into piece-level SHA-1 hashed blocks, implements a Kademlia Distributed Hash Table (DHT) over UDP for decentralized peer discovery, executes rarest-first piece downloading over concurrent TCP connections, and enforces tit-for-tat choking algorithms to incentivize reciprocal bandwidth sharing.

use_cases.title: Large-Scale Container Image & Software Update Distribution
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise infrastructure teams deploying multi-gigabyte container images across thousands of bare-metal server nodes need to avoid saturating central container registries.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine distributes images peer-to-peer across cluster nodes, enabling servers to download pieces from neighboring rack servers and reducing central registry egress bandwidth by over 80%.

use_cases.title: Decentralized Open-Source Dataset Distribution
use_cases.first_sentence: Machine learning research consortiums sharing multi-terabyte scientific datasets require resilient distribution channels that do not depend on expensive cloud bucket hosting.
use_cases.second_sentence: Researchers share dataset torrent manifests, discovering peers via Kademlia DHT and transferring verified data blocks across distributed academic nodes with cryptographic integrity.

use_cases.title: Edge CDN Cache Re-Seeding & Bandwidth Offloading
use_cases.first_sentence: Content delivery network operators distributing high-demand video chunks to regional edge Points of Presence (PoPs) face heavy transit backhaul costs.
use_cases.second_sentence: The P2P network allows regional edge servers to re-seed and exchange cached video blocks horizontally across local fiber interconnects without fetching redundant copies from origin storage.

hard_parts: Implementing the Kademlia DHT routing table with 160-bit XOR distance metrics and iterative node lookup algorithms over UDP
Designing concurrent TCP peer wire protocol state machines managing handshake, bitfield, request, piece, and keep-alive frames
Implementing rarest-first piece scheduling algorithms that optimize piece availability across the swarm without duplicate downloads
Enforcing reciprocal choking/unchoking algorithms (tit-for-tat) to maximize upload and download bandwidth efficiency while preventing free-riding
screener_signals: Clean Go codebase adhering to systems design best practices, separating DHT routing, TCP peer state machines, and disk block managers
Swarm benchmark report demonstrating >= 2.4x download speedup across a 5-node swarm compared to single-source HTTP transfers
Anti-fake verification script injecting an intentionally corrupted binary piece from peer B and verifying the client detects hash failure and re-downloads from peer C

architecture.data_flow: The client loads a metainfo .torrent file, extracts the 20-byte infohash and piece hashes, and allocates disk space; the Kademlia DHT module queries neighboring nodes over UDP to find peers announcing the target infohash; the client establishes concurrent TCP connections to discovered peers, exchanges handshakes and bitfields; the rarest-first scheduler identifies pieces with the lowest frequency across connected peers and requests 16KB sub-blocks; received blocks write to disk; upon receiving all sub-blocks for a piece, the SHA-1 hasher validates integrity; if valid, the client updates its bitfield and announces piece availability to the swarm; when a peer disconnects, the scheduler transparently reassigns pending blocks.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Cryptographic SHA-1 verification on every piece discarding corrupted bytes; Kademlia k-bucket replacement rules keeping active nodes.

targets.environment: Go test harness simulating Byzantine peer injecting corrupted byte payloads
targets.minimum_pass: 20 of 20 corrupted pieces detected by SHA-1 hash and re-downloaded with 0 corrupted bytes in final file
targets.target: 20 of 20 corrupted pieces detected by SHA-1 hash and re-downloaded with 0 corrupted bytes in final file
targets.report: Cryptographic piece verification audit log and corruption recovery report

targets.method: Verification of complete file transfer when 2 of 5 seeding peers suddenly terminate connections mid-download

targets.minimum_pass: File transfer reaches verified data integrity confirmed by SHA-1 hash across the piece set
targets.target: File transfer reaches verified data integrity confirmed by SHA-1 hash across the piece set

prerequisites: Proficiency in Go systems programming, socket networking (net.Conn, net.PacketConn), and goroutines
Understanding of P2P network architectures, BitTorrent wire specifications, and cryptographic hashing

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU and network I/O bound systems software)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Go 1.21+ and Docker Desktop (for multi-peer swarm) installed
environment.fallback_path: Running 5 peer instances as local OS background processes communicating across loopback ports

riskiest_component.name: Deadlocks and Goroutine Leaks in Peer State Machine Sockets
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce strict read/write socket timeouts, context cancellation propagation, and buffered channels for peer message queues.
riskiest_component.fallback: Centralized supervisor goroutine terminating unresponsive peer connections after 30-second silence.

Screener verification script executing automated benchmark and dynamic corrupted piece recovery in under 3 minutes
out_of_scope: Copyrighted media indexing, tracker torrent search engines, or public swarm scraping
NAT traversal using UPnP / NAT-PMP port forwarding protocols on physical residential routers
Custom video player streaming playback codecs

rubric.input: 20 corrupted piece blocks injected into incoming peer data streams
rubric.expected_result: SHA-1 hasher detects all 20 corrupted pieces, discards bytes, and re-downloads valid pieces
rubric.evidence_location: Piece integrity audit log in reports/integrity_audit.json
rubric.pass_criterion: 20 of 20 corrupted pieces rejected and final file SHA-1 matches ground truth with exit code 0

rubric.input: Sudden termination of 2 seeding peers at 50% download progress
rubric.expected_result: Engine reassigns missing piece blocks to remaining peers and completes 100% of download
rubric.pass_criterion: File transfer completes with valid SHA-1 checksum and exit code 0

rubric.input: CLI request querying active peer swarm status and bitfield progress
rubric.expected_result: CLI outputs connected peer list, download rate, upload rate, and bitfield completion percentage
rubric.pass_criterion: Output displays active peer count >= 3 and valid completion progress with exit code 0

rubric.input: Dynamic corrupted piece injected from peer 2 while piece 3 is transferring
rubric.expected_result: Client logs 'SHA1_MISMATCH: Piece 3 corrupted', requests piece from peer 3, and verifies valid hash
rubric.evidence_location: Dynamic verification console execution output log
rubric.pass_criterion: Console confirms piece 3 rejected from peer 2, re-downloaded from peer 3, with exit code 0

worksheet.q2: Target users: distributed systems engineers, network protocol software developers, and core infrastructure architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: container image cluster distribution, decentralized open-source dataset sharing, and edge CDN cache re-seeding.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: Kademlia 160-bit XOR routing tables over UDP, binary peer wire protocol state machines, rarest-first piece scheduling, and tit-for-tat choking algorithms.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: .torrent parser, Docker 5-node test swarm, and 100MB synthetic test payload. Synthetic binary test files only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: 5 local loopback background processes.
